teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). All three are official teaching languages of the programme and admission is language-position based, not language-specific. English is genuinely used (e.g. the mathematics preparatory course is held in English; 'Refreshing English' 2 CP in year 1 and 'Scientific Writing in English' 6 CP in year 2 are compulsory), but Italian and German carry equal official weight, and the two compulsory 'Foreign Language 1 / Foreign Language 2' course pairs (3+3 CP in year 1, 3+3 CP in year 2) are explicitly German/Italian-as-a-foreign-language specialised language courses. Students who graduated in a language other than the three official teaching languages must nominate the two languages in which they will sit the language exams. unibz does not publish a percentage split of teaching hours per language for this programme. [uncertain]
campus: Bozen-Bolzano (main campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). Faculty of Economics and Management. Single campus — no NOI Techpark, Brixen, Bruneck or external-site component.
degree_class: L-18 (Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale / Economics and Business Administration). Confirmed on the 2026/27 official brochure: 'Bachelor class: L-18'. The admission PDF also references L-18 when explaining the double-enrolment rule.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and fully run in 2026/27. Both the Early Bird and Late Application sessions were completed and signed ranking lists were published (130 EU + 2 non-EU admitted in Early Bird; 38 EU admitted in Late). IMPORTANT EXCEPTION: the programme was NOT included in the Additional Application Session (18/08–04/09/2026) — the additional-session page lists it as 'Application NOT offered'. So for 2026/27 only two intake windows existed for this programme.
is_new_programme: No. This is a long-established flagship programme of the Faculty of Economics and Management; published unibz ranking lists for this degree exist at least as far back as 2017 (Ranking-List-2017-2nd-Bachelor-Economics-management-L-18.pdf). The exact first intake year is not stated on the official pages. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: No formal majors, tracks or separate study plans — one single 180 ECTS / 3-year study plan for all students. Specialisation happens only in year 3 through structured electives: (a) three 'Typical Subject' slots, each a choice of one out of four — Accounting group (Intermediate Financial Accounting / Management Accounting and Control / Auditing / Artificial Intelligence for Accounting and Finance), Management group (Entrepreneurship and Innovation Management / International Management / Management of SMEs / Human Resources and Organization), Finance group (Financial Risk Management / Financial Systems and Financial Markets / Banking and Corporate Finance / International Finance); (b) one Complementary Subject from Econometrics for Economics or Econometrics for Finance; (c) three further Complementary Subjects from a list of eleven (Contract Law, Bankruptcy Law, Law of Banking and Finance, Public and Administrative Law, Italian Accounting Standards, Financial Statement Analysis, Operations Management, Nature and Society, The Economics of Climate Change, Applied and Behavioral Economics, Philosophy of Economics). Plus 12 CP of Free Choice Courses taken in year 2 or 3. The brochure summarises the focus areas as econometrics, business economics, accounting and management. Part-time enrolment is available as an administrative variant (reduced course load, full access to services), not as a separate study plan. A compulsory internship of at least 150 hours (6 CP) is part of year 2.
english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for an English-only candidate. Admission requires B2 in the FIRST language and B2 in the SECOND language, where the three languages are German, Italian and English. A candidate who can only certify English can satisfy at most one of the two required positions and will be excluded from the admission procedure before ranking — this is not theoretical: the 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list excludes a named block of applicants (including 8 non-EU applicants) explicitly 'for not meeting the language requirements for admission', and the Late list excludes 34 more on the same ground. A Turkish or other international applicant therefore needs a certified B2 in German OR Italian in addition to English. Only the third language may be left uncertified at entry (though B1 is then needed to sit exams in it, and B2 is the graduation requirement). Classification: effectively-closed.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with competitive ranking. No entrance examination, no TOLC, no SAT, no interview and no portfolio. Selection is a document- and grade-based dossier evaluation performed by the Admission Committee on the basis of self-declared secondary-school grades plus language-certificate bonus points. Applications are submitted through the unibz Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/). Separate quotas and procedures apply to (1) EU citizens and those given parity of treatment and (2) non-EU citizens living abroad. Selection criteria approved by Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025.
academic_requirements: Secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system, OR an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if it was obtained after 12 years of education AND at least the last two years were attended within that foreign school system (unibz gives the Irish Leaving Certificate as the counter-example: attending only one year and obtaining the certificate is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain qualifications — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly — and applicants in those categories are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service) before applying. No specific subject prerequisites, no minimum GPA gate other than the ranking threshold, and no prior ECTS/SSD requirement (this is a bachelor programme, so the SSD-credit logic that applies to unibz master admissions is not relevant here). Candidates who have not yet graduated may apply and upload the diploma at enrolment. Under national rules, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of two programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same degree class (e.g. not L-18 with another L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of course content. Language requirements (see language section) are a hard admission gate — failing them means exclusion from the procedure before any ranking.
entry_exam_or_test: NO admission entrance exam of any kind — unibz does not use its own subject test, TOLC-I, TOLC-E, CENT-S, SAT or GMAT/GRE for this programme. Admission is purely dossier/ranking based.

Language proficiency exams (optional route, only if you cannot prove your levels by diploma or recognised certificate): organised online by the unibz Language Centre. 2026/27 Early Bird sittings 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 + 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late Application sittings 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Registration is done inside the application portal under 'enrol for language exams'. Note: only B2-level exams can be booked.

Compulsory mathematics test — AFTER admission, not for admission. The faculty runs a mathematics preparatory course in English before the first semester (2026/27: 21–25/09/2026) and every new student must sit a compulsory test at the end of it. A negative result or non-participation triggers OFA (see ofa_rules). Test topics are published at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Economics/OFA-Topics26.pdf (English only).
Third-language placement test — after admission, for students who cannot certify their third language; determines the assigned language-learning path.
selection_scoring: Maximum 33 points, minimum 21/33 required for admission; the final score is rounded up or down. Component (a) — up to 30 points from the grade average of the last two available high-school years (the last two if the final year is already available, otherwise the two years preceding the final year), expressed in thirtieths. For each of those years the candidate supplies one mark for each of four subject areas: 1) Language (any, modern or ancient), 2) Mathematics, 3) Humanities and Social Sciences (history, philosophy, politics, sociology, economics, law), 4) Natural and Technical Sciences (physics, chemistry, biology, geography, environmental studies, informatics); plus 2 further marks from areas 1, 3 or 4. If a subject area cannot be filled, a grade from another area may be substituted. Excluded from the calculation: conduct (condotta/Betragen), religion, physical education, performing-arts subjects (instrumental music, singing, drama/theatre) and hospitality-sector subjects (cuisine, restaurant and bar service, oenology). Component (b) — up to 3 language bonus points (see bonus_points). Tie-breakers: higher grade average first, then the younger applicant. If the candidate does not supply grades for a year, the Committee assigns a score corresponding to 'sufficient merit' for that year; for school systems substantially different from the Italian one the Committee may evaluate reports from other years; if the candidate already holds a university degree, the Committee uses the university exam average. ACTUAL 2026/27 CUT-OFFS (competition signal): Early Bird EU — top score 32.00, 130th and last admitted 23.25, waiting list ran from rank 131 down to 20.50, applicants at 20.49 and below were excluded for not reaching the minimum. Early Bird non-EU living abroad — only 2 admitted, scores 23.09 and 22.73. Late Application EU — top score 31.49, 38th and last admitted 24.50, waiting list to rank 74 (20.75), excluded from 20.25 downward.
bonus_points: Maximum 3 bonus points, awarded solely for language proficiency ABOVE the required admission level, on this scale: C1 + C1 + at least B2 = 3 points; C1 + C1 + B1 = 2.5 points; C1 + C1 = 2 points; at least B2 + B2 + B2 = 1 point; at least B2 + B2 + B1 = 0.5 points. Only language certificates recognised by the unibz Language Centre count, as do exams taken at the Language Centre provided a course for the requested level is offered. NO other bonus schemes apply to this programme — there is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is a Master in Software Engineering / Computing for Data Science mechanism), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), and no startup-project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation).
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter, no CV and no reference letters are part of this admission procedure — and therefore no format/size limits apply. The only uploads are identity document, self-declared grades (entered in the portal form), scanned school report cards where the years were completed abroad, official translations of the report cards into Italian/German/English where needed, optional language certificates, and the diploma (at application if already held, otherwise at enrolment).
interview: No interview. The admission procedure contains no oral or online interview stage at any point, for either EU or non-EU applicants, and no interview dates are published for this programme.
conditional_admission: Yes, in the bachelor sense: applicants who have not yet completed secondary school may apply and are ranked on the grades of the two years preceding the final year. The diploma is then uploaded at enrolment rather than at application. The ECTS-threshold form of conditional admission (>=120 ECTS, 140 for Data Analytics) does not apply here — that is a unibz master's mechanism. Financial protection: if you pay the first instalment to secure your place but then fail your secondary-school final exam, you ARE entitled to a refund (this is one of only two refund exceptions, the other being non-EU applicants abroad who fail to obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities). Non-EU citizens living abroad are additionally admitted 'with reservation' (con riserva / mit Vorbehalt) on the ranking list — the reservation is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. Missing the fee-payment or enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next person on the ranking list is admitted.
ofa_rules: Yes — OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional study achievements) applies to this programme. OFA is assigned to any student who fails, or does not attend, the compulsory mathematics test held at the end of the September mathematics preparatory course. Three alternative ways to clear it: (1) pass the test offered at the end of the OFA exercise sessions, (2) pass the exam at the end of teaching module 1 of the 'Mathematics' course, or (3) pass the full mathematics exam (teaching module 1 + teaching module 2) within the first academic year. Consequence of not clearing OFA: the student is blocked from sitting the quantitative examinations of years 2 and 3 — specifically Statistics, Financial Mathematics, Econometrics for Economics and Econometrics for Finance. Test topics: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Economics/OFA-Topics26.pdf
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and language requirements are a hard exclusion gate — failing them means exclusion from the admission procedure before ranking, not a lower score. Requirements are defined by POSITION (1st/2nd/3rd language), not by which language: your first language is the one you are strongest in, your third is the one you are weakest in or an absolute beginner in. Entry: B2 in the 1st language, B2 in the 2nd language, no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and only recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. A B1 in the third language is the minimum to sit curricular exams in that language, and if the first semester is taught only in English while English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January to take all first-semester exams. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2; three-week intensive courses run in September (2026/27: 01–18/09/2026, Mon–Fri, 6 h/day) and A1 beginner courses are now offered ONLY in that September window, so absolute beginners must start there. Extensive courses (4 h/week) run during semesters, intensive courses (6 h/day) between semesters. Higher-than-required levels earn up to 3 ranking bonus points.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required at entry. (Pattern B2/B2/none.) The positions are self-assigned by proficiency across German, Italian and English, so any two of the three languages may fill positions 1 and 2. Conditional follow-on: B1 in the 3rd language is required to sit curricular examinations in that language, and B1 in English by mid-January if English is your 3rd language and your first semester is English-only. Note that only B2-level exams can be booked at the unibz Language Centre, so a candidate needing to prove C1 for bonus points must bring an external recognised certificate.
exit_levels: 1st language: C1 — 2nd language: C1 — 3rd language: B2. CEFR levels. This is the standard unibz trilingual exit pattern and it is a graduation condition: a student admitted with B2/B2/none must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in the third before graduating. The Language Centre's free course path is calibrated to this (B1 in the third language by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2).
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Special case flagged by unibz: if the first semester of the programme is taught only in English and English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January in order to sit all the curricular exams scheduled for the first semester. Students who cannot certify the third language on admission take a placement test and are assigned a learning path aimed at reaching B2 as quickly as possible.
proof_pathways: Four accepted routes, all handled inside the application portal (sections 'upload language certificates' and 'enrol for language exams', available only after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'): (1) The main teaching language of your FINAL high-school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1. Ladin upper-secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian. For foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma you must also upload a letter from the school stating it. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; same medium-of-instruction letter rule for foreign degrees; unibz graduates upload their Language Centre certificates or declare the B2/B2+/C1 exams they passed. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf); if it cannot be uploaded it may be emailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre — 2026/27 online sittings: 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026), 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026) for Early Bird, and 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026) for Late Application; only B2-level exams can be booked, and no Language Centre exams are held during the Additional Application Session. Fifth partial route for bi-/multilingual and foreign schools: if the diploma explicitly states CEFR levels (B1/B2/C1) for German, Italian or English AND all four skills were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language — upload the school leaving certificate under the respective language and the Language Centre decides on recognition. Formalities: certificates from an Italian public institution are submitted as a self-declaration; certificates from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scan of the original.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 (Beschluss des Universitätsrates / Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università 16/2026). Core rules: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must show an adequate result in every skill as an overall grade, or the detailed per-skill assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall level is stated, the LOWEST level reached in any sub-skill determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed; (4) there is NO compensation for failed parts and no averaging unless the issuer itself provides for it; (5) certificates obtained as remote 'home edition' exams are NOT recognised, except for those explicitly flagged in the list; (6) single-skill certificates combined from different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational providers, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers or teachers are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are explicitly NOT recognised. Validity: an international certificate must have been obtained within the last five years at the time of submission — counted as the whole calendar year, i.e. certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth year preceding submission remain valid for the entirety of that year. Items listed in the 'Further proofs / Ulteriori attestati / Weitere Nachweise' section of the document have unlimited validity.
application_deadline_eu: Two sessions were open for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment in 2026/27; the third (Additional) session was NOT offered for this programme. (1) EARLY BIRD — application 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08, by noon local time (28/05 - 08/07/2026). Applicants excluded in the first session may re-apply in the second, and EU applicants may apply to more than one study programme. (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION — window 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04 university-wide, but the additional-session page lists Bachelor in Economics and Management as 'Application NOT offered', so this route did not exist for this programme in 2026/27. NOTE: as of the verification date (2026-08-29) the entire 2026/27 cycle is closed; 2027/28 dates are not yet published.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (Early Bird, unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have no Late Application and no Additional Session — 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies. Downstream 2026/27 dates were the same as Early Bird: ranking by 2026-05-27, first instalment by 2026-06-05 (noon), enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 (noon). Universitaly pre-enrolment is mandatory after paying the first instalment, and admission on the ranking list is granted 'with reservation' until the Italian consulate confirms directly to unibz.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU-equivalent and therefore get access to the Late Application session and the larger EU quota. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and Vatican City State. (2) Non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay (permesso di soggiorno) under article 39 paragraph 5 of Decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — issued for WORK, FAMILY reasons, political or humanitarian ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. They apply directly to the University and must upload a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. CRITICAL FOR TURKISH AND OTHER NON-EU APPLICANTS: a permit to stay for STUDY reasons and a tourism visa are NOT sufficient. If the permit is not uploaded in the application portal, the applicant is automatically reclassified as a non-EU citizen living abroad and pushed into the Italian-consulate procedure with the much smaller quota (5 places vs 150).
places_quotas: Three separate numbers for 2026/27, total 155. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: 130 in Early Bird + 20 in Late Application = 150. Non-EU citizens living abroad: 5, Early Bird only. Any places from the Early Bird round left unfilled by EU/equivalent candidates roll over into the Late Application round for EU/equivalent candidates. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN 2026/27 (competition signal): Early Bird admitted exactly 130 EU/equivalent candidates with a waiting list running to rank 167, and admitted only 2 of the 5 available non-EU places (scores 23.09 and 22.73) while 8 further non-EU applicants were excluded for not meeting the language requirements; the Late session then admitted 38 EU candidates (20 base quota plus 18 rolled-over places) with a waiting list to rank 74. Waiting-list candidates were contacted by email from 06/06/2026 (Early Bird) and 07/08/2026 (Late).
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD 2026/27 — ranking lists published by 2026-05-27; first instalment of tuition fees (which is what secures the place) by 2026-06-05 noon local time; waiting-list candidates contacted by email from 2026-06-06; enrolment window 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 noon. LATE APPLICATION 2026/27 — ranking lists published by 2026-07-30; first instalment by 2026-08-06 noon; waiting-list candidates contacted from 2026-08-07; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-08-06 noon. Missing the payment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next candidate on the list is admitted; missing the enrolment deadline has the same effect. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of two places by paying the designated rate twice. Paying does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol, except if you fail your secondary-school final exam or (non-EU abroad) cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. Ranking lists are valid for the respective academic year only. Note the faculty-level fee calendar differs from the admission calendar once enrolled: first instalment due 13/10/2026 and second by 31/03/2027 per the Faculty of Economics fee page.
programme_specific_dates: 2026/27 calendar from the programme's own admission-information PDF. Language exams (online): 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026); 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Intensive language courses: 01–18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 h/day. Mathematics pre-courses: 21–25/09/2026, followed by the compulsory mathematics test. Freshers Days: 28–29/09/2026. 1st semester classes: 28/09–23/12/2026 and 07–23/01/2027; extraordinary exam session 10–23/12/2026; winter holidays 24/12/2026–06/01/2027; exams 25/01–20/02/2027. 2nd semester classes: 01/03–25/03/2027 and 30/03–12/06/2027; Easter holidays 26–29/03/2027; extraordinary exam session 12–22/05/2027; exams 15/06–10/07/2027. Autumn exam session: 23/08–25/09/2027. No programme-specific entrance exam, interview or portfolio deadline exists for this programme.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION (uploaded in the unibz Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) a valid ID card or passport, front and back — an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document means exclusion from the admission procedure; (2) the completed online application form, including self-declaration of the grades for the four subject areas plus two extra subjects for each of the two relevant high-school years (German secondary schools: the 'Jahreszeugnis' grades, or the average of the two 'Halbjahreszeugnisse' with decimal place if unavailable); (3) a copy of the relevant school report cards where a self-declared year was completed abroad; (4) official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; (5) optionally, language certificates for the bonus-point calculation and for proving entry levels; (6) the diploma of the qualification if already obtained (otherwise at enrolment). Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Once sent, the application cannot be modified, and forms that are filled in but not correctly submitted are disregarded. AT ENROLMENT, for a foreign secondary-school qualification: the diploma; an official Italian translation (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. NOTE: the structured 'study career' Excel template that unibz requires for master's applications is NOT part of this bachelor procedure. Transfer students from another Italian university must additionally submit a copy of the transfer application filed at their previous university to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. unibz may request further documents in case of doubt and can exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the admission qualification is not valid.
application_fee: EUR 50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living abroad. It is an administration fee and is non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/economics-management/fees — EUR 1,200 per year for students within the normal programme length, split into two instalments of EUR 600. The 1st instalment includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and, in the admission procedure, is the payment that secures the admitted place (2026/27 admission deadlines: 05/06/2026 Early Bird, 06/08/2026 Late). Once enrolled, the faculty fee calendar is 1st instalment by 13/10/2026 and 2nd instalment by 31/03/2027 (the admission PDF states more generally 'by March of the following year'). Late payment of the second instalment incurs a EUR 30 fine and blocks exam registration and mySNS access; unpaid fees also block transfer to other universities or programmes. Students beyond the normal programme length (fuori corso) pay EUR 1,500 (EUR 900 + EUR 600). No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Full exemption (paying only the EUR 16 stamp) for students with a disability recognised under art. 3 para. 1 of Law 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more — the health-authority certificate must be handed in at the start of the academic year — and for foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Holders of a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees, usually in March–April.
scholarships_grants: (1) Provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, applied for via the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario: approximately EUR 1,680 to EUR 6,960 per year depending on income, and holders also get their unibz tuition fees refunded. [uncertain — amounts taken from the unibz Study Guide and may be updated for the 2026/27 call]. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS: a non-EU student can apply for the provincial grant only if holding a long-term residence permit, or after having been resident in South Tyrol for at least one full uninterrupted year — so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa is effectively excluded from it in year 1. (2) Merit-based scholarships: from the second year onwards, students with an exam grade average of 27/30 can apply on merit rather than income. (3) Tuition-fee exemption for Italian-government scholarship holders and for students with a recognised disability (see tuition_or_fees_link). (4) The student associations sh.asus and MUA assist with the grant application. No programme-specific scholarship is advertised for the Bachelor in Economics and Management on its own page. Source: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: Required at ENROLMENT for holders of a foreign secondary-school qualification, in three tiers. (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate: Statement of Correspondence of the secondary-school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database – Italy). (b) Non-EU countries that are signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence from ARDI PLUS Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence). (c) Non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA PLUS Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. In all cases the diploma itself and an official Italian translation must be uploaded — the translation is not needed for diplomas issued in German or English. The 12-years-of-education rule and the last-two-years-in-that-school-system rule (see academic_requirements) apply. unibz performs its own checks and may request additional documents; an invalid admission qualification can lead to exclusion by Rector's decree even after enrolment. The 180-ECTS Diploma Supplement evidence mentioned in the field definition applies to master's admissions, not to this bachelor. Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so Turkish applicants fall under tier (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. [uncertain — tier assignment for Turkey is inferred from Lisbon Convention membership; unibz does not publish a country-by-country table]
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window with the EUR 50 fee -> ranking list published (admission granted 'with reservation') -> pay the 1st instalment to secure the place -> start the visa application on the Universitaly portal, which is MANDATORY (without it you will not be allowed to enrol) and on which you may select ONE study programme only -> the Italian diplomatic/consular authorities in your country issue the study/university entry visa and send official confirmation directly to unibz, which lifts the reservation -> enrol at unibz. unibz warns explicitly that admission does not create any right to a visa (that is the exclusive competence of the Italian consular representations) and that holding a visa does not create any right to enrol. Proof of means of subsistence for the visa: roughly EUR 800 per month of living costs in Bozen-Bolzano excluding tuition, with a total of at least EUR 36,000 to be demonstrated for a bachelor programme (EUR 24,000 for a master), and the budget should also cover health insurance and visa costs. After arrival: the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) must be applied for within 8 working days — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and the permit must then be handed in at the Student Office in person or by email. Work is capped at 20 hours per week / 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay but cannot obtain the necessary enrolment documents from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund.

source_quotes: Places (admission-information PDF, 'Available places'): 'EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — Early Bird Application: 130; Late Application: 20. Non-EU citizens (living abroad) — Early Bird Application: 5.'
Threshold (admission-information PDF, 'Admission procedure'): 'Applicants have to reach at least 21/33 points to be admitted to the programme.'

Language gate (admission-information PDF, 'Language requirements'): entry level '1st language: B2, 2nd language: B2, 3rd language: no level required'; exit level '1st language: C1, 2nd language: C1, 3rd language: B2'.
Non-EU single window (admission-information PDF): 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: EUR 50.'
Bonus scale (admission-information PDF): 'C1+C1+ at least B2 = 3 points; C1+C1+B1 = 2.5 points; C1+C1 = 2 points; at least B2+B2+B2 = 1 points; at least B2+B2+B1 = 0.5 points.'

Actual cut-offs (Early Bird ranking list PDF, 2026/27, 1st session): 130 EU/equivalent admitted, rank 1 score 32.00, rank 130 score 23.25; 'Le persone dalla posizione numero 131 risultano in lista d'attesa' with the waiting list running to rank 167 (20.50); non-EU section admitted 2 people, scores 23.09 and 22.73.
Actual cut-offs (Late Application ranking list PDF, 2026/27, 2nd session): 38 EU/equivalent admitted, rank 1 score 31.49, rank 38 score 24.50, waiting list from rank 39 to rank 74 (20.75).
Legal basis (both ranking-list PDFs): selection criteria 'approvati con la delibera del Consiglio di Facolta della Facolta di Economia n. 142 dd. 15.09.2025'.

Certificate rules (Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026): 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive'; 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam (home edition) are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list'; DAAD certificates are not recognised; international certificates must have been obtained within the last five years.

OFA (admission-information PDF): failure to complete the additional achievements means 'students will not be allowed to take the examinations in the quantitative subjects of the second and third years of study (Statistics, Financial Mathematics, Econometrics for Economics and Econometrics for Finance)'.

Additional session (https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/additional-application-session): Bachelor in Economics and Management is listed as 'Application NOT offered' for the 2026/27 additional session (18/08-04/09/2026).

Parity of treatment (admission-information PDF): a permit to stay is valid for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum or religious reasons — 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient.'
Tuition (admission-information PDF): 'Fees amount to EUR 1200. 1st instalment (EUR 600): includes the revenue stamp of EUR 16. 2nd instalment (EUR 600): must be paid by March of the following year.'

Degree class and profile (2026/27 brochure, 'At a glance'): 'Bachelor class: L-18; ECTS credits: 180; Duration of the course: 3 years; Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual); Places available: 150 EU + 5 non-EU; Campus: Bozen-Bolzano; Tuition fees: ca. EUR 1200 per year.'
uncertainty_notes: 1) CYCLE STATUS — all data here is the 2026/27 cycle, which is already CLOSED as of the verification date (2026-08-29): both application windows have passed, both ranking lists are published and signed, and the additional session did not include this programme. The 2027/28 call, quotas and dates are not yet published; expect the same structure (Early Bird ~early March to late April, Late ~late May to early July) but treat every specific date above as historical rather than actionable. 2) The two official PDFs both carry 'Latest update: 24.08.2026' and are explicitly marked 'Subject to change'. 3) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING is not published — unibz states the programme is trilingual and the study plan shows which language courses are compulsory, but no percentage split of teaching hours by language is given anywhere, and the course-level language assignment is not stated on the public study plan page. The teaching_language field is therefore marked uncertain on the weighting only; the trilingual classification itself is certain. 4) FIRST INTAKE YEAR is not published; the 'not a new programme' assessment rests on ranking lists existing at least back to 2017. 5) OFFICIAL CALL — there is no standalone English call/manifesto PDF; Faculty Council Resolution 142/15.09.2025 is cited in the ranking lists but not downloadable, so official_call_url is a best-effort answer. 6) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS (EUR 1,680–6,960) come from the unibz Study Guide rather than the current provincial call and may be a prior-year figure. 7) TURKEY'S CREDENTIAL TIER (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification) is inferred from Turkey's Lisbon Convention membership; unibz publishes the rule by tier, not by country, so Turkish applicants should confirm with apply@unibz.it. 8) The faculty fee-calendar dates (13/10/2026 and 31/03/2027) come from guide.unibz.it and are slightly more specific than the admission PDF's 'by March of the following year' — no contradiction, different granularity. 9) The ranking-list PDFs are published only in Italian and German; the English admission PDF does not report cut-off scores, so all cut-off figures were read from the bilingual IT/DE ranking documents. 10) An English-only applicant is treated here as effectively excluded — this is an interpretation of the B2/B2 position rule, but it is corroborated by the large exclusion blocks 'for not meeting the language requirements' in both 2026/27 ranking lists (8 non-EU and dozens of EU applicants).
